# `Q-9-6` — Multiple XML Root Elements

> The XML document contains more than one top-level element.

## What this means

A well-formed XML document has exactly one root element. This
error fires when the parser, after finishing the first
top-level element, finds another element at the document's top
level instead of end-of-input.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **Two documents concatenated** without a wrapping root.
- **A stray closing tag** that prematurely ended the intended
  root, leaving the rest of the content at top level.
- **Hand-edited XML** where a wrapping element was deleted by
  mistake.

## How to fix

Wrap the top-level elements in a single container, or remove
the spurious element if it does not belong. The message names
the location where the second root element starts — that is
where to look.

## Related

- `Q-9-5` — empty XML document: no root element at all.
- `Q-9-4` — invalid XML structure: other structural constraints
  the parser enforces.
